UnitStatement: Document title: VALIDATION STRATEGY - Harness Runtime and Governance Evidence.
Status: Draft governance support surface.
Product scope: the Chirality desktop harness and bundled agent operating system.
This validation strategy applies to app-dev governance, harness runtime, frontend validation, packaging evidence, and governed workspace workflows.
This document defines how Chirality App validation evidence is classified, collected, and interpreted, and routes evidence for app-dev work.

Validation evidence does not replace docs/DIRECTIVE.md, docs/CONTRACT.md, docs/SPEC.md, docs/TYPES.md, docs/PRD.md, docs/PLAN.md, source code, tests, accepted execution artifacts, decision records, or git history.

Validation evidence is software and governance evidence only; it is not lifecycle issuance, release publication authorization, professional approval, certification, sealing, authentication, code-compliance acceptance, or external validation for reliance.
Chirality separates evidence into five evidence classes.

Static governance evidence proves control-plane links, stale-rule removal, plan/log consistency, decision-register routing, and clean documentation diffs; it does not prove runtime behavior, release readiness, or human approval.

Runtime contract verification proves product-owned adapter, session, event, permission, SDK isolation, and tool-surface behavior under deterministic tests; it does not prove professional adequacy or future SDK behavior after an untested upgrade.

Harness workflow validation proves API and UI-facing harness workflows behave as expected against a running local app surface; it does not prove full user acceptance, all platform packaging behavior, or release publication readiness.

Packaging and instruction-root evidence proves required instruction-root resources are present and packaged build commands complete where applicable; it does not prove signed, notarized, published, or externally distributed release status.

Boundary and claims review proves network, API-key, redaction, professional-boundary, and product-identity constraints remain visible and enforced; it does not prove legal advice, professional-practice advice, or code-compliance approval.
Evidence must bind to the command run, working tree state or commit, affected files, generated artifacts where applicable, and skipped checks with reasons.
A skipped check is acceptable only when the tranche scope makes the skip explicit and defensible.
Unless a tranche specifies narrower validation, app-dev validation commands are run from frontend/.
`npm run test` runs Vitest unit and contract checks for API routes, runtime libraries, SDK mapping, tool descriptors, session events, UI helpers, script policies, and governance helpers.
`npm run typecheck` is a TypeScript contract check for frontend and Electron entry surfaces.

`npm run harness:validate:premerge` runs running-app harness workflow validation with a stable summary artifact at frontend/artifacts/harness/section8/latest/summary.json and requires the harness API to be reachable.
`npm run instruction-root:integrity` checks instruction-root packaging/resource integrity with a summary artifact at frontend/artifacts/harness/instruction-root-integrity/latest/summary.json.
`npm run proof:network-policy` proves the network policy for the current shipped loopback plus Anthropic outbound policy.
`npm run build` produces Next/Electron build evidence for source and Electron entry surfaces.
`npm run desktop:pack` produces unsigned local macOS arm64 directory packaging plus instruction-root integrity.
`npm run desktop:dist` produces unsigned/unnotarized local-builder macOS arm64 DMG plus instruction-root integrity.
Documentation-only governance tranches normally use static checks instead of frontend runtime commands.
Runtime, SDK, permission, network, packaging, and release-significant tranches use the applicable gate family in docs/RELEASE_QUALITY_GATES.md.
Build, packaging, artifact, and release-evidence command details are recorded in docs/BUILD_AND_RELEASE.md.

For coordination, plans, decision-register pointers, or docs-only governance changes, minimum evidence is git diff --check over affected docs/control-plane paths, targeted rg checks for retired rules or stale authority, link/path existence checks for new references, and an explicit no-runtime-code-change check.

For runtime engine contract, adapter, turn lifecycle, session events, or event schema changes, minimum evidence is focused Vitest coverage for touched runtime modules, npm run typecheck, and broader npm run test when shared contracts move.

For SDK options, permission overlay, tool descriptors, tool exposure, MCP wrappers, or hooks changes, minimum evidence is focused tests for options, permissions, descriptors, denied tools, and unknown tools, plus npm run typecheck and broader tests when exposure semantics change.

For harness API, running workflow, session boot, SSE, interrupt, attachment, or validation behavior changes, minimum evidence is relevant unit/API tests, npm run harness:validate:premerge against a reachable local app, and summary artifact review.
For network, API key, redaction, or provider policy changes, minimum evidence is relevant unit tests, npm run proof:network-policy, and redaction or key-storage tests where touched.

For UI workflow, professional-boundary copy, product identity, or navigation changes, minimum evidence is relevant component/library tests, targeted manual or browser review when layout/copy behavior changes, and no prohibited professional/release claims.

For instruction-root, bundled resources, Electron packaging, release scripts, or distribution metadata changes, minimum evidence is npm run instruction-root:integrity, npm run build, and npm run desktop:pack or npm run desktop:dist when packaging behavior changes.

For future domain-engine adapters or operation proposals, minimum evidence is runtime tests plus explicit human-gate and professional-boundary review, with no direct protected-domain writes unless a governed adapter workflow authorizes them.
Machine-readable artifacts are preferred when available.
The harness premerge summary artifact is at frontend/artifacts/harness/section8/latest/summary.json.
The instruction-root integrity summary artifact is at frontend/artifacts/harness/instruction-root-integrity/latest/summary.json.
Test command output is captured in terminal or run records when required by a tranche.
Plan/log closeout pointers are in plans/PLAN_2026-06-13_runtime_completion.md and plans/PLAN_COMPLETION_LOG.md.

Evidence artifacts are derivative records that support review and regression analysis but do not become decomposition truth, product requirements, lifecycle approval, release authorization, or professional acceptance.
Hosted CI provider, workflow location, and public/private data handling remain governed future decisions.
Final release-label vocabulary, signing, notarization, publication, and attestation remain governed future decisions.
Final coverage, performance, and platform-matrix thresholds remain TBD.
Concrete provider/network implementation beyond the current shipped Anthropic path requires a bounded future implementation tranche and recorded decision evidence.

D-APP-01 and D-APP-02 rule Pi pattern-corpus-only: no Pi adapter, fork, package import, Node 22 sidecar, runtime-floor migration, or spike work unless a future ruling explicitly reverses those boundaries.
